# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to communicate what I see to Mute and Blind, but I can't hear anything back yet. Blind can't see gestures or writing, so I can only reach Blind through speech directly, or relay info that Mute can read out... wait, Mute can't speak either. Let me think about who can talk: only I (Deaf) can speak, and Blind can speak too? No - checking roles: Mute cannot speak, Blind cannot see/hear-related restrictions weren't listed as "cannot speak". Let me recheck: Blind's cannot column only says "see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - so Blind CAN speak. Mute cannot speak. I (Deaf) - my cannot column says "hear anything, or touch the bomb" - it doesn't say I can't speak, so I can speak.

So speech works: Deaf speaks, Blind speaks. Mute is silent but can hear (no restriction on hearing listed) and can gesture. I should speak the display info to both Mute and Blind since this is turn order Mute->Blind->Deaf, meaning my speech now will reach next round's Mute and Blind.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Display shows 9. Light is green. Wires in order: 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Waiting on manual info from Mute and what Blind can feel.")
wait()
```

TURN 2

DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured a thumbs up to me - likely acknowledging receipt or signaling something simple like "understood" or "matches manual" but I don't have context for what it maps to yet. I don't know what Mute's manual says, so I should wait for Blind or Mute to give more info via speech (from Blind) or gestures. Since Mute can't speak, they can only gesture to me. I should keep feeding info and ask Blind (who can speak) to relay what they feel, and see if Mute can gesture more specific things once Blind speaks constraints.

Let me prompt Blind to describe what they feel, since Blind can speak and I can hear Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Display 9, light green, wires in order 1 white 2 green 3 red 4 yellow 5 purple. Please describe what you feel - number of wires, textures, switches, anything - so Mute can match it to the manual.")
wait()
```

```

Mute keeps gesturing thumbs up - possibly confirming they understood my description, or trying to signal something about the manual matching. Since Mute can't speak and I can't interpret gestures without established meaning, I need Blind to speak up with details so Mute can react with gestures I can interpret in context, or so Blind can tell me directly what to do.

I should wait for Blind's speech since Blind should have received my request by now (it was sent after Blind's turn in round 2, so it arrives at start of round 3 for Blind). Let me check - Blind speaks in round 3 after receiving my round 2 message. That speech would then reach me at start of round 4... but I see nothing from Blind yet, only Mute's gesture repeated.

Let me continue waiting but also try prompting again in case Blind missed it or needs more explicit ask.

```

(empty)

Still nothing from Blind. Let me reconsider the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf - each round. My speech in round 2 (as Deaf, last in that round) would land on whoever comes after me "in that same round" - but I'm last, so it reaches Mute and Blind at the start of round 3.

In round 3, Blind acts (after Mute). Blind should have received my message asking them to describe what they feel. Blind would then speak, and that speech lands on whoever comes after Blind in round 3, which is me (Deaf). So I should have received Blind's speech at the start of round 4. But I got nothing except Mute's gesture repeated (maybe stale/same gesture shown again, not new).

Wait, the arrivals said "(empty)" for turn 3 and turn 5, and Mute's gesture appeared in turn 2 and turn 4 - possibly this is just showing state each time rather than only new events. Let me just continue prompting Blind directly and also try to acknowledge Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here, still waiting to hear from you. Please speak up: how many wires do you feel, any switches or buttons, anything you can describe by touch.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

Still nothing. Let me try a different approach - maybe Blind isn't speaking because they don't know they should, or maybe there's an issue. Let me re-send the full bomb description in case earlier messages got lost, and be very explicit about needing a response.

```
speak(text="Deaf here, repeating for both: Display 9, light green, 5 wires in order: 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Blind, please speak and tell me what you physically feel on the bomb - count of wires, any buttons, switches, textures. Mute, if you have manual info, gesture it to me using the symbol alphabet, one gesture per piece of info, and I will relay in speech to Blind.")

```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute changed their gesture from 👍 to 🤟. This is a new signal - possibly Mute is trying to establish a code with me since we can't have prearranged meanings. This could mean anything, but the change itself suggests responsiveness to my message. 

Since Mute cannot speak and I cannot see manual, we need a gesture-based code. Perhaps Mute is trying to indicate something like "wire 3" or a step number using gesture symbols as a substitute for numbers/letters. Without prior agreement, I can't decode this reliably, but I should try establishing a simple mapping.

Let me propose an explicit gesture code to Mute for numbers 1-5 (matching wire positions) and colors, so Mute can point to which wire matches manual instructions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see 5 wires numbered 1 to 5, colors white green red yellow purple, display 9, light green. If you want to tell me which wire to cut, gesture the number of touches matching its position - one gesture for wire 1, two for wire 2, etc. Use thumbs up count as the number, like this: one symbol equals wire 1, two symbols equals wire 2, and so on. If manual says something about display 9 or green light, gesture differently, like a wave for display and a point for light.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Mute gestured three thumbs-up symbols. Following the code I just proposed (though this response likely reflects Mute's answer to my *previous* message, not this one, due to timing lag), three symbols could mean "wire 3" if using my proposed counting scheme. That would point to the red wire.

However, I need to be careful about timing - this response was likely to my turn 6 message (the "speak up" one) or an even earlier one, not my turn 8 code proposal, since that proposal was just sent this round and Mute wouldn't have received it yet when producing this turn's gesture.

Actually let's reconsider: my turn 8 message was sent as Deaf (last in round 8), so it reaches Mute at start of round 9. Mute acts first in round 9, so this gesture [👍 👍 👍] is Mute's reaction to my turn 8 code proposal. That's a strong signal - three thumbs up = wire 3 = red wire, using my proposed count code.

I should confirm this interpretation and relay to Blind, but I want to be cautious - let me ask Mute to confirm before relaying an action to Blind, since a wrong cut kills everyone.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I think you are telling me wire 3, the red wire. If that is correct, gesture one thumbs up only next turn. If wrong, gesture a different symbol, like a wave, instead.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with a single thumbs up - this matches my confirmation request (one thumbs up = correct, wire 3/red is right). This is a strong signal that wire 3 (red) is the correct wire to cut according to the manual.

Now I need to relay this to Blind, who can hear my speech.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire number 3, the red wire. Confirmed with Mute using a counting code. Wire 3 is red.")

```

This is progress. I need to report this new state and see if further action is needed. Let me inform both Blind and Mute of the updated board so Mute can check the manual for the next step (display 4, light yellow).

```
speak(text="Wire 3 cut successfully. New display shows 4, light is now yellow. Remaining wires: 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Mute, please check manual for what to do next given display 4 and yellow light, then gesture the wire number using thumbs-up count as before, or a different gesture if the action isn't a wire cut.")
wait()
```
